overview: ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private sector bank by assets, offering retail, SME/business banking, corporate and international banking alongside treasury operations, through a network of over 7,650 branches and digital platforms including iMobile Pay and InstaBIZ. The bank also controls a diversified group of financial-services subsidiaries spanning life and general insurance, asset management, securities broking and home finance, giving it fee-income streams beyond the core lending and deposit-taking business. Reporting is standalone on the NSE (ICICIBANK.NS); the same entity's ADRs trade in New York as IBN.

business_model.summary: Core earnings come from net interest income on a loan book split roughly evenly between retail/rural (~52%), business banking/SME (~21%) and domestic corporate (~19%), funded by a CASA- and term-deposit base; non-interest income (fees, FX, treasury) and dividends/consolidated profits from insurance, AMC and securities subsidiaries add a recurring, less capital-intensive layer on top.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C (retail mortgages, personal loans, credit cards, vehicle/jewel loans) and B2B (SME/business banking, corporate, trade finance); retail and rural loans are ~52% of the domestic book, business banking ~21%, domestic corporate ~19%, overseas/international ~8%
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly India (~90% of consolidated advances domestic); international book via branches in GIFT City/overseas plus wholly owned subsidiaries ICICI Bank UK and ICICI Bank Canada; overseas book has grown sharply (to ~10% of advances) partly via FCNR(B)-deposit-funded lending

main_competitors: Bank of Baroda / other PSU banks
competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest private bank by assets and among the largest by market capitalisation; in 2026 has closed much of its market-cap and Nifty-weight gap with HDFC Bank on the back of superior margins, profitability and asset quality, while remaining smaller than SBI on a pure balance-sheet basis

moat_factors.description: 7,656 branches (up from 6,983 a year earlier) plus ~12,100 ATMs give deep retail reach across metro, urban, semi-urban and rural India
iMobile Pay (tens of millions of users, including customers of other banks), InstaBIZ, DigiEase and iLens reduce servicing cost and improve cross-sell and underwriting speed

Net NPA ratio of 0.30% and provision coverage of 75% (Sep 2026), low top-20-borrower concentration (6.3% of exposure), and CET1 of 16.0% give capital headroom competitors with weaker asset quality lack

Majority or significant stakes in ICICI Prudential Life, ICICI Lombard General Insurance, ICICI Prudential AMC (market leader in equity AUM), and ICICI Securities create cross-sell and a sum-of-the-parts value the bank captures that pure lenders do not
CEO Sandeep Bakhshi's reappointment through October 2028 (RBI-approved May 2026) signals strategic continuity after the post-2018 turnaround from the Kochhar-era governance issues

weaknesses: Net interest margin is compressing (4.18% in Q2 FY2027 vs 4.36% in Q1 FY2027) as repo-linked loans (~57% of the domestic book) reprice down faster than deposits
CASA ratio has slipped (average CASA ratio down to 35.8% in Q2 FY2027 from ~39% a year earlier), raising reliance on costlier term deposits
Recent loan and deposit growth is partly inflated by FCNR(B) deposit-funded overseas lending (ex-FCNR loan growth 24.1% vs headline 30.0% y-o-y), which carries FX/ALM and hedging-cost complexity
Credit card outstanding has contracted y-o-y (-9.7%), reflecting continued caution on unsecured retail credit after the 2023-24 RBI-driven tightening cycle
Treasury income is volatile and turned negative in Q2 FY2027

growth_drivers: Continued under-penetration of retail credit (mortgages, personal loans, vehicle, jewel loans) in India supports double-digit retail book growth (retail and rural +14.8% y-o-y)
Business banking/SME lending is the fastest-growing segment (+33.8% y-o-y), driven by InstaBIZ, Merchant STACK, Trade Online and digital onboarding (DigiEase, EazySign)
Domestic corporate lending re-acceleration (+30.6% y-o-y) as capex cycle and M&A/acquisition financing (RBI eased acquisition-financing norms effective April 2026) pick up

Subsidiary value creation: ICICI Prudential Life's Value of New Business up ~22% y-o-y in H1 FY2027; ICICI Prudential AMC's QAAUM up 14.4% y-o-y to ₹11.6 trillion with market-leading equity/hybrid AUM share; ICICI Lombard premium growth
Enterprise AI adoption (GenAI customer service, document intelligence, fraud detection, underwriting/iLens) targeted at efficiency, turnaround time and fraud prevention
Branch network expansion (+673 branches in the last 12 months) and rural/jewel loan penetration (jewel loans +79.4% y-o-y) extend reach into semi-urban and rural India
International/GIFT City book and NRI deposit (FCNR) franchise provide an additional, though lower-margin, growth lever

business.risk: Asset-quality cyclicality in unsecured and priority-sector retail
business.description: An additional standard-asset provision of ₹12.83bn was taken in the agricultural priority-sector portfolio pursuant to RBI's annual supervisory review; Kisan Credit Card additions remain a recurring source of gross NPA formation

business.risk: Intensifying competition for deposits and retail credit
business.description: HDFC Bank, SBI, Axis and Kotak all compete aggressively for CASA deposits and retail/SME loans, pressuring pricing and funding costs industry-wide
UPI apps (PhonePe, Google Pay) dominate payments volume even where ICICI provides the underlying rails, limiting monetisation of payment market share

financial.description: NIM fell to 4.18% in Q2 FY2027 from 4.36% in Q1 as ~57% of the loan book re-prices with the RBI repo rate while term-deposit costs lag down more slowly; management flagged the FCNR(B)-driven CASA dilution would fully show up in Q3 FY2027

financial.risk: FX/ALM exposure from FCNR-funded overseas book
financial.description: Overseas advances jumped from ₹332bn to ₹1,430bn in two quarters, funded largely by FCNR(B) deposits with a landed cost (including hedges) cited by analysts near 6.5%, raising basis and rollover risk if NRI deposit flows reverse
Treasury income swung to a loss of ~₹2.3bn in Q2 FY2027 from a gain in prior quarters

regulatory.description: RBI's 2025-26 overhaul of project-finance provisioning, credit-risk capital charges, acquisition financing and securities-backed lending limits continues to reshape capital and provisioning requirements across the sector; any tightening of retail unsecured-lending risk weights would disproportionately affect banks with larger unsecured books

CEO Sandeep Bakhshi's new term (Oct 2026-Oct 2028) has RBI approval but still required shareholder ratification as of mid-2026; the bank operates under heightened RBI scrutiny of private-bank governance following the 2018 Kochhar-era issues
IRDAI and SEBI rule changes (e.g., insurance surrender-value norms, AMC expense ratios) can compress subsidiary profitability that flows into consolidated and SOTP value

macro.description: RBI repo-rate cuts compress NIM given the repo-linked share of the loan book; a prolonged easing cycle would continue to pressure margins industry-wide
A slowdown in consumption or corporate capex would reduce credit growth and could reverse the current benign retail asset-quality trend
FX moves affect the overseas/FCNR book and foreign portfolio flows into Indian bank stocks, which have driven much of ICICI's re-rating versus HDFC Bank

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Indian private-bank credit growth has reaccelerated into double digits in 2026 (ICICI total loans +30% y-o-y, +24% ex-FCNR) after a period of RBI-driven deceleration in unsecured retail; system deposit growth and CASA mix remain structurally challenged versus loan growth, keeping funding costs elevated
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - credit growth and asset quality track the Indian GDP and rate cycle; ICICI's diversified, granular book and high provision coverage dampen downside versus peers with concentrated corporate or unsecured exposure
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - NIM is directly exposed to RBI repo-rate moves given ~57% of the domestic loan book is linked to repo/external benchmarks versus stickier deposit repricing

recent_developments.event: Q2 FY2027 results: standalone PAT up 20.1% y-o-y to ₹148.43bn (beating consensus of ~₹142.5bn); core operating profit up 21.8% y-o-y to ₹208.05bn; shares fell despite the beat on NIM compression concerns, while brokerages (PL Capital, Elara, Motilal Oswal/Nomura) largely stayed bullish
Net NPA ratio improved to 0.30% (from 0.35% at Jun 2026) and provision coverage rose to 75.0%; gross NPA ratio down to 1.20%
Total deposits grew 27.1% y-o-y (17.0% ex-FCNR) and total loans grew 30.0% y-o-y (24.1% ex-FCNR), with overseas book expanding sharply on FCNR(B)-funded lending; average CASA ratio fell to 35.8%
RBI approved Sandeep Bakhshi's reappointment as MD & CEO for a further two-year term (Oct 4, 2026 - Oct 3, 2028), pending final shareholder approval

Key subsidiaries continued to scale: ICICI Prudential Life's Value of New Business rose ~22% y-o-y to ₹12.83bn; ICICI Prudential AMC's QAAUM grew 14.4% y-o-y to ₹11.6 trillion, retaining market-leading equity and equity-hybrid AUM share; ICICI Securities' MTF market share reached ~16.1%

RBI finalised a package of prudential reforms (eased project-finance provisioning effective Oct 2025, revised credit-risk capital charges, higher acquisition-financing and securities-backed lending limits effective April 2026) reshaping capital requirements across Indian banks, generally capital-accretive for large banks including ICICI
ICICI Bank's market capitalisation and Nifty 50 index weight closed in on HDFC Bank's, with ICICI shares outperforming HDFC Bank year-to-date as HDFC's margins and CASA mix lagged

items.target: No specific numeric target disclosed; management indicated the FCNR(B)-driven CASA/margin dilution would be fully reflected in Q3 FY2027 before stabilising
items.vs_prior: lowered (implicitly, versus the 4.30-4.36% levels of the prior two quarters)
items.notes: NIM fell to 4.18% in Q2 FY2027 from 4.36% in Q1 FY2027; management did not provide a specific exit-NIM number

items.target: Normalised credit cost expected to run up to ~50 bps of advances
items.notes: Reported Q2 FY2027 credit cost was ~20bps, flattered by one-off corporate recoveries; management cautioned against extrapolating the low reported figure
Management declined to give specific credit-growth guidance on the Q2 FY2027 call, noting continued granular, risk-calibrated growth across retail, business banking and corporate segments

items.target: Maintain CET1 comfortably above regulatory minimums to fund growth without equity dilution
items.notes: CET1 of 16.01% at Sep 30, 2026 provides substantial buffer versus regulatory requirements

guidance.management_commentary: Management emphasised 'Return of Capital' discipline and risk-calibrated, granular growth rather than headline loan growth targets. On the Q2 FY2027 call, management attributed the quarter's margin decline to the temporary drag from FCNR(B) deposit inflows diluting the CASA mix, expected to fully play out by Q3 FY2027, after which margins should stabilise/improve; the Q2 treasury loss was characterised as normal quarterly volatility rather than a trend.

bull_case: Industry-leading profitability among large Indian banks: standalone ROA of ~2.3-2.5% and consolidated ROE near 17%, alongside best-in-class asset quality (net NPA 0.30%, PCR 75%)
Strong capital position (CET1 ~16%) funds continued double-digit loan growth without needing dilutive equity raises

Diversified, fast-growing subsidiary franchise (life and general insurance, market-leading AMC, securities broking) adds a sum-of-the-parts value layer and reduces reliance on pure net interest income
Management continuity through 2028 (Bakhshi reappointment) and broad sell-side support (the large majority of covering analysts rate the stock Buy/Strong Buy)
Narrowing valuation/market-cap gap with HDFC Bank and rising Nifty weight reflect structural market-share gains in deposits and advances
bear_case: Net interest margin is in a clear downtrend (4.18% in Q2 FY2027 vs 4.36% in Q1) as repo-linked assets reprice faster than deposits in an RBI easing cycle, with no firm management target for stabilisation
Declining CASA ratio (down to ~36%) and growing reliance on costlier term and FCNR(B) deposits raise structural funding costs and FX/ALM complexity

Recent headline loan and deposit growth is partly a function of FCNR(B)-funded overseas lending rather than organic domestic demand, masking a softer underlying (ex-FCNR) growth rate (~24% vs 30% headline)

Regulatory risk remains elevated as RBI continues to recalibrate prudential norms (unsecured lending, project finance, priority-sector provisioning), any of which could raise capital or provisioning requirements
Valuation already prices in much of the quality premium versus HDFC Bank, SBI and Axis, leaving less room for multiple expansion if growth or margin trends disappoint
